classification.classification_note: The saved ASan trace shows a read-after-free in `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal` after XInclude fallback handling stores fallback children in the include table and later frees those same nodes before document serialization walks namespace fields on the retained list.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal (xmlsave.c): during XInclude processing (xmlXIncludeIncludeNode in xinclude.c) namespace/node structures are freed (via xmlFreeNs/xmlFreeNode) while they are still reachable and later accessed by document-dumping functions (xmlDocContentDumpOutput / xmlDocDumpFormatMemoryEnc). This use-after-free can cause crashes and memory corruption, with potential for exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The testcase drives libxml2 through XML parsing and XInclude fallback processing. `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` stores copies of `fallback->children` into `ctxt->incTab[nr]->inc`, but vulnerable `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` later iterates `cur->children` and frees those fallback nodes before the include list is reinserted. Because the retained `list` still aliases the freed nodes, later document dumping reaches `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal`, which reads `cur->ns->prefix` or `cur->nsDef` from freed node/namespace storage and triggers the ASan heap-use-after-free.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled XML start tag and attributes into parser state that will allocate the namespace node later retained through XInclude fallback.
source.value_from: The saved ASan allocation stack shows the crashing namespace object was allocated by `xmlNewNs` from `xmlSAX2AttributeInternal` while the testcase was parsed through `xmlParseStartTag`/`xmlParseElementStart`/`xmlParseDocument` before XInclude processing and serialization.

root_cause.description: The include node frees fallback children even though `list = ctxt->incTab[nr]->inc` still holds aliases to the same nodes for later reinsertion.
root_cause.note: The fix removes this stale-alias situation by copying fallback children into `incTab[nr]->inc` and by moving fallback-child removal before reinsertion in a way that no longer frees the nodes later inserted. The vulnerable path violates the lifetime obligation that nodes reachable through `list` must remain live until reinsertion is complete.

sink.description: Serializer dereferences namespace data from a node that remained reachable after being freed during XInclude fallback cleanup.
sink.note: ASan reports the first invalid read at `xmlsave.c:897:48`, corresponding to the `cur->ns->prefix` access inside `xmlNodeDumpOutputInternal`.

tainted_value_origin.note: The harness provides attacker-controlled XML bytes, but the scored source is the first downstream project parser statement that consumes them.

parser_admitted.description: After document setup and start-tag parsing succeed, the XML parser enters element parsing on the testcase document, which is necessary for the later namespace allocation and XInclude tree processing.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The attacker-controlled element start tag and attributes are parsed into project state. The ASan allocation stack shows this parsing path reaches `xmlSAX2AttributeInternal`, which allocates the namespace object later involved in the UAF.
Namespace state derived from the testcase is allocated on the heap and attached to the parsed node. The saved ASan report records this allocation as the origin of the later freed namespace object.
The XInclude fallback path stores the fallback child list into the include table, making those parsed nodes the replacement list that `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` will later consume.

Root-cause step. After `list = ctxt->incTab[nr]->inc`, the function still iterates `cur->children` and frees each fallback child. On the vulnerable path the nodes referenced by `list` are therefore freed while the include replacement list still points to them.
The include replacement loop reloads each node pointer from the retained `list` after the cleanup loop, turning the stale container entry into a local pointer that is treated as a live node.
Document serialization walks the document children after XInclude processing and passes the previously reinserted stale node pointer into the recursive dumper.

Sink step. The dumper dereferences namespace data through the stale node pointer. ASan records the first invalid read here, 24 bytes into a 48-byte region previously freed by `xmlFreeNs` from `xmlFreeNode` in `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode`.

format.name: libxml2-xml-fuzzer
format.contract: A fuzz target input for `fuzz/xml.c` whose XML document drives XInclude processing down the fallback path so that `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` stores fallback children, `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` frees those same nodes, and later document dumping serializes the stale replacement list. The verified trigger semantics are this XInclude-fallback witness, not generic XML without that fallback aliasing path.
